name: TX-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 11-point partisan lean
Incumbent Veronica Escobar running with a large fundraising edge
No general-election polling, but markets price Escobar at 98%
Republican challenger Adam Bauman has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Escobar is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 11 points, and prediction markets give her roughly a 98% chance of winning. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a surge of outside spending against Escobar would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Veronica Escobar seeks another term in a heavily Democratic El Paso-area district that leans 11 points toward Democrats. She has raised about $859,000 and holds a cash advantage, while Republican Adam Bauman reports no fundraising. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the incumbent's financial edge. Prediction markets price Escobar's chances at roughly 98%, consistent with a comfortable double-digit expected margin. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the confidence level moderate despite the lopsided fundamentals.
